title: Restock areas and vehicles
summary: Supermarket Simulator treats bringing stock in as its own job: the game defines restock areas for boxes and a separate area for vehicles, so where you unload decides how much work a delivery is.
body: Unloading is placed in the shop rather than happening automatically, and the game keeps a dedicated area for boxes you bring in.
Vehicles get their own restock area, which is why a delivery can be handled on foot or moved with hardware depending on how the shop is laid out.
Because the entrance and its surrounding area can change, the distance between the door and the shelf is something you choose rather than something you inherit.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the icon it ships for one of the vehicles that can carry stock, so what the vehicle area is for is pictured rather than only named.
What this entry does not tell you: how large an area is, how much a vehicle can carry or how many boxes fit. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: There is a dedicated restock area for boxes.
Vehicles have their own restock area, separate from the box area.
The shop entrance is managed and can change.
There are helper items that carry jobs of their own.
The game ships its own icon for one of the vehicles that carries stock.
